baseRigs._note: The rigs as constructed by each set BEFORE applyAtmosphere mutates them. applyAtmosphere overwrites key colour/intensity (and position only when the preset carries keyPos), rim intensity only, and hemisphere colour/ground/intensity. Shadow parameters, rim colour/position, key target and environmentIntensity are never touched by a preset.

colourLaw: Colours are the source hex strings. three.js Color.set on a '#RRGGBB' string stores the sRGB-decoded linear components; the hex string is the canonical source value.

dynamics._note: Everything env.ts / engine.ts / shots.ts COMPUTES rather than stores. Formulas are written out in ATMOSPHERES.md; these are the machine-readable summaries.
dynamics.applyAtmosphere: env.ts:164-216. scene.fog = preset.fog ? Fog(color, near, far) : null. Unless sky === false: every Sprite's material colour = preset.cloudTint; every ShaderMaterial with top/hor/gnd uniforms gets preset.skyTop/skyHor/skyGnd. If rig given: key.color = preset.keyCol, key.intensity = preset.keyI, key.position = preset.keyPos ONLY IF the preset has one; rim.intensity = preset.rimI (rim colour untouched); the HemisphereLight inside rig.group gets preset.hemiSky/hemiGround/hemiI. Then every Toon in the scene with envMatch === true gets matchEnv(preset.tint). The preset is returned; its grade reaches the render ONLY where a shot feeds it via gradeOf (fog/golden/dusk shots) - noon shots never consult preset.grade.
dynamics.fireLevel: shots.ts:287-291. level in [0,1], t = film time (seconds, global t - not shot-local). vis = level > 0.02; both flame meshes visible = vis. If vis: f = 1 + 0.16*sin(13t) + 0.07*sin(29t + 1); flame.scale = (level, f*level, level); flame2.scale = (level, (2-f)*level, level); fireLight.intensity = (4.6 + 0.7*sin(17t) + 0.5*sin(7.3t)) * level. Else fireLight.intensity = 0.
dynamics.fireTo: shots.ts:190-194. An earlier boolean variant (visible = lit; scale (1, f, 1) / (1, 2-f, 1); intensity 4.6 + 0.7*sin(17t) + 0.5*sin(7.3t), no level factor). DEFINED BUT NEVER CALLED - every shot uses fireLevel. Recorded so the native port does not mistake it for the live path.
dynamics.focus: shots.ts:127-131 (shoot). Per frame: focus = cam.position.distanceTo(current look target) where the target is the shot's at/at2 point mixed by the same camera k. BokehPass focus therefore tracks the subject distance continuously during push-ins and cranes.
dynamics.gradeOf: shots.ts:139: gradeOf(base, p) = { ...base, sat: p.grade.sat, warm: p.grade.warm, exposure: p.grade.exposure }. Only sat/warm/exposure cross over; bloom/aperture/maxblur/vignette/grain always stay the shot grade's.
dynamics.gradeShader: engine.ts:20-24. d = vUv - 0.5; d.x *= 0.5625; rgb *= 1 - uVig * smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, length(d) * 1.4); rgb += (hash(vUv * 1000.0) - 0.5) * uGrain where hash(p) = fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(12.9898, 78.233)) + uTime * 7.13) * 43758.5453); r += uWarm * 0.5; b -= uWarm * 0.5; l = dot(rgb, vec3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114)); rgb = mix(vec3(l), rgb, uSat). uTime = 0 for this entire film (nothing sets look.t), so the grain term is a fixed per-pixel offset.
dynamics.matchEnv: toon.ts:664-674. Given tint t: r=1+0.6*t.warm; g=1; b=1-0.6*t.warm. If t.sat<1: k=(1-t.sat)*0.25; each channel c += (0.92-c)*k. e=clamp(sqrt(max(t.exposure,0)),0,1.15); all channels *= e. If t.fogMix>0: colour = lerp(colour, fogColor, clamp(t.fogMix,0,1)). The result REPLACES the toon material colour (body plane + head plane). For the noon identity tint this evaluates to exactly (1,1,1).
dynamics.skyDome: world.ts:149-155. Fragment: y = normalize(position).y; c = y > 0 ? mix(hor, top, pow(clamp(y*1.6, 0, 1), 0.7)) : gnd. Material: BackSide, depthWrite false, fog false, toneMapped false, sphere r=380, renderOrder -10.

bloomPass.filmValues: No film shot sets bloomThreshold; threshold is 0.85 and radius 0.6 in every shot. Strength comes from the shot grade (shotGrades).

bokehPass.filmFocusRule: shots.ts shoot() always passes focus = camera.position.distanceTo(lookTarget) for the current frame (shots.ts:127-131); see dynamics.focus

engine.environmentMap: PMREMGenerator.fromScene(new RoomEnvironment(), 0.04) - one shared envMap for all sets (engine.ts:37)

gradePass.filmTimeSeed: No code path in shots.ts or main.ts ever sets look.t, so uTime = 0 for every frame of this film: the grain hash is a FIXED spatial pattern, not animated. See dynamics.gradeShader.

filmLooks._note: The EFFECTIVE, fully-merged parameter set per shot group - what the native engine must reproduce frame for frame. Merge rules (see dynamics): noon shots use their shotGrade verbatim (preset grade NOT consulted); fog/golden/dusk shots merge preset grade over the shot grade via gradeOf (sat/warm/exposure only) and then apply the shot's literal overrides. Rig values are baseRig AFTER the preset's mutations. Sky values are the dome uniforms AFTER dressing (or the set's own when sky:false).

key._posNote: position IS the preset keyPos: it replaces the JG sunlight position [7,12,5] for this shot (and persists in the shared rig until the next applyAtmosphere with a keyPos or set rebuild).

name: onoda-film-atmospheres
numberLaw: All numbers are the exact decimal literals appearing in the TypeScript source. Each literal parses (f64) and narrows to the identical f32 the source produces at runtime; no value is a decimal approximation of a computed quantity. Quantities the source COMPUTES (fire intensity, bokeh focus, grade merges) are not sampled here - their formulas are in the 'dynamics' block and in ATMOSPHERES.md.

presets._cite: src/core/env.ts ATMOSPHERES (env.ts:62-141). Verbatim preset objects. keyPos is ABSENT (not null) where the source omits it: applyAtmosphere then leaves the rig's key position untouched.

fog._filmNote: S06 applies this preset and then REPLACES scene.fog with its own values in the same draw call - the preset fog below is never rendered. The effective fog is in filmLooks.jg-fog-s06.fog. The preset GRADE and TINT do reach the render (grade via gradeOf + a sat override).

provenance: Every value transcribed first-hand from the project's src/core/env.ts (ATMOSPHERES presets), src/core/engine.ts (post chain + lightRig), src/core/world.ts (sky/sunlight/interior) and src/shots.ts (set construction, per-shot looks, overrides). Full citations per value group are in scenes/ATMOSPHERES.md.

shotGrades._cite: shots.ts:134-138 (const G). These are RenderLook fragments: bloom = UnrealBloomPass strength, aperture/maxblur = BokehPass, sat/warm/exposure feed the GRADE pass and tone mapping exposure, vignette = GRADE uVig, grain = GRADE uGrain.
